message.content:
Test file: src/game-of-life.spec.ts
Failing test: "should bring a dead cell with exactly three live neighbors to life"
Expected behavior: a dead cell with exactly 3 live neighbors becomes alive — the result must contain [1, 1]
Current error: AssertionError: expected [ [ +0, +0 ], [ +0, 1 ], [ 1, +0 ] ] to deep equally contain [ 1, 1 ]
Implementation file: src/game-of-life.ts

Root cause is structural, not arithmetic: `nextGeneration` is `livingCells.filter((cell) => survives(cell, livingCells))`, so its output is always a subset of its input. The minimal fix must widen the candidate set to include dead neighbors of living cells and apply the birth rule (exactly 3 live neighbors) to them.

Note: cells are `[number, number]` tuples, so identity/dedup comparisons must be by value, not by reference.

EXPERIMENT MODE: Run autonomously, proceed to Refactor after completion.

content.text:
All 6 active tests pass, 4 remain as `it.todo`.

🟢 Green Phase Complete:
**Implementation**: `/home/experimenter/experiments/runs/2026-07-25_23-19-54_game-of-life-example-mapping_v4-exact-subagents_opus-5/src/game-of-life.ts` — widened the candidate set from `livingCells` to `livingCells` plus every neighbor of a living cell (deduplicated by value via `isSameCell`/`contains`), and split `survives` into two branches: a living candidate needs 2 or 3 live neighbors, a dead candidate needs exactly 3.

**Result**: All tests now pass (6 passing, 4 todo)

**Approach**: This is the minimal fix for the structural problem the failing test exposed. Filtering `livingCells` can only ever return a subset of the input, so no arithmetic tweak could produce `[1, 1]` — the candidate set had to grow. Dead cells outside the neighborhood of a living cell can never have 3 live neighbors, so bounding candidates to living cells plus their neighbors is the smallest widening that works; no grid, bounding box, or coordinate normalization was introduced. Dedup and the living-cell check use value comparison because cells are tuples, per the note. The birth rule is a plain `=== 3` with no generalization beyond what the current test demands.

Proceeding to Refactor phase.
